verdict: screened: static best 27.32 fast (score 90.07, CMA C, compliant 10-deg stops; gate converged 0.06/0.01/0.01) is made of relay ISLANDS - with continuity enforced (connect=1: the arm must be able to move into the pose) the same shape scores 31.92 (score 88.39), rocker locked 32.63: the relay is worth 0.71 points; kinematic ceiling over 72 pivot directions +0.023 big-bench reach, +0 overhead. Worse than the zero-passive leader it sits on (spine-parked 28.49 fast / 34.29 verified) at +13.5 complexity; J1's MVP2 reaction (0.87 tau1 on a 0.2 N.m spring) trips the rocker. Recommend: drop (connect-objective CMA H-K and frozen exact were queued on the farm).
limiter: the relay entry: at the switch the rocker sub-chain (c, u1, u3; arcs beta, lo) sits at its own fold for the entries the CMA favours (margin 1.4-8.7 deg over 6 frames, then a 30-deg q0 jump); where entries are regular, the overhead poses lie on the OTHER closure root (q0 -49.5 -> +44.2 between elevation 90 and 120), unreachable without J2 passing its stop. mechanism.notes: spine-parked spherical 3R with J1 carried by a passive rocker R0 (pivot axis through GH). bodies: rocker, link 1, link 2, arm-end (member 3: hub-3 plate + K7 neck rigid on BOTTOM). joints: R0 (O15 slim hub, MR117-2RS pair, AS5600 + magnet: SENSED, the rocker angle must be read in modes B/C to know the arm pose), J1 (O20), J2 (O15, with an O2 dowel in a 103-deg arc slot = its two hard stops), J3 (O15). Centring: ONE centring element (a double-torsion spring, or a V-cam + spring-plunger detent) counted as 1 spring; two opposed single torsion springs would count 2. Open chain closed by GH: Kutzbach M = 4 with the spring + stops determining q0 (force closure, R17 checked in the doc). custom: base, rocker, 2 links, arm-end plate + neck, 4 hub shafts (9, est.); catalogue: 4 x MR117 pair, 1 spring (or plunger), J2 stop dowel + 2 PEEK pads (est. 8; sensor parts not counted).
